editorial.headline: Private Domestic-Work Training Is Open Nationally and in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 85576 covers privately run vocational training for domestic-work roles, with all business scales open and full foreign ownership available nationally.
editorial.body:
Private domestic-work training is the practical core of this activity: privately organised vocational instruction designed to build skills for household managers, elderly carers, infant and toddler carers, child carers, cooks, and related roles. Its focus is not the provision of domestic services themselves, but the training that equips people to undertake that work with greater skill and expertise. That distinction gives the activity a clear professional purpose, centred on capability-building for occupations that sit close to household life and care.

The activity is open across the full range of stated business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the record does not confine private training to a single commercial form or a narrow operating size. A small training provider and a larger institution can each sit within the same activity, provided their work remains the delivery of the specified private vocational training. For a founder, the essential question is therefore whether the enterprise is genuinely organised around training people for these roles, rather than around a different service proposition.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is straightforward. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, foreign ownership can reach 100% at the national level. The underlying PMA references listed in the record are Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021.

Bali does not reverse that national openness. The activity is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali, and its Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason is specific: at the Besar scale, the OSS risk classification is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by Bali’s moratorium. That moratorium permanently blocks PMA for Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the province, but the record expressly says it does not block this one. The honest conclusion is therefore a clean one: this private domestic-work training activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the stated moratorium rule.
